candidates.title: PRT player copies and keccak-hashes the guest-declared tx-buffer payload (up to 2 MiB) at every automatic yield of its claim pass, decoupled from guest work: ~5 ms (local) / ~60 ms (JSON-RPC) per yield vs ~30-130 us for the emulator's own collection
candidates.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (prt.lua run_next_input -> run_to_input_mcycle_offset -> run_to_stop/on_yield_automatic), with the Lua binding of receive_cmio_request (clua-i-machine.cpp, remote path asks for a worst-case 2 MiB buffer); the cartesi-machine CLI (get_and_print_yield in its run_to_stop) shares the pattern
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes, the cartesi-machine CLI ... Support'); it stands in for the honest operator (an implementation of an operator that computes claims). The Lua/JSON-RPC receive_cmio_request API itself behaves as documented and is not the defect.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua: run_next_input (~2242-2272, always passes last_output = {}), run_to_input_mcycle_offset (~2065-2124: defines on_yield_automatic whenever last_output is given; for TX_OUTPUT does keccak(output_data), lines ~2083-2091), run_to_stop (~1397-1410: for every yielded_automatically break calls receive_cmio_request(machine), which reads min(htif_tohost_data, 2 MiB) of the tx buffer for any automatic reason, reports and unknown reasons included); prt.lua receive_cmio_request (~972-976). src/clua-i-machine.cpp machine_obj_index_receive_cmio_request (~1300-1335: for a JSON-RPC machine requests CM_AR_CMIO_TX_BUFFER_LENGTH so the server base64-encodes the whole declared payload); src/machine.cpp machine::receive_cmio_request (~1986-2016: available_length = min(tohost DATA, AR_CMIO_TX_BUFFER_LENGTH), the guest-declared length). Same pattern: src/cartesi-machine.lua run_to_stop/get_and_print_yield (~4561-4570, 3309-3325).
candidates.description: While computing its mcycle claim (run_next_input builds the epoch's computation hash with the mcycle builder), the player services every automatic yield by calling machine:receive_cmio_request(), which copies min(DATA, 2 MiB) bytes of the tx buffer into a Lua string, where DATA is the 32-bit length the guest wrote in tohost; for reason TX_OUTPUT it then keccak256-hashes that string. The guest need not write anything to the tx buffer: one 'sd' of tohost = yield|automatic|TX_OUTPUT|0x200000 in a 2-instruction loop yields every 2 mcycles and makes the host copy 2 MiB and hash 2 MiB per yield. Over JSON-RPC (the in-memory player's new_machine/fork_server machines) the Lua binding always asks for the 2 MiB worst case, and the server base64-encodes and JSON-serializes it. None of this is needed to compute the claim: section 4 says output payloads are opaque guest data that the transition function does not interpret, and the emulator's collector does not read them. So the per-yield host cost of the claim pass is set by a guest-declared length rather than by guest work, and it multiplies the per-yield cost of building part of a claim by about 170x (local, the stored player of crisium.lua) to about 470x (JSON-RPC, the in-memory player). The comparison is with the same claim pass that does not read payloads (the emulator's collect_mcycle_root_hashes alone). Reports (TX_REPORT) and unknown automatic reasons pay the full copy (about 0.7 ms local, about 57 ms over JSON-RPC) and their data is then discarded.
candidates.trigger: Guest code after reading an input (fully adversarial for containment, section 4): any input that takes control of the application runs a loop of automatic yields with reason TX_OUTPUT (or TX_REPORT) and DATA = 0x200000, at 2 mcycles per yield, for as many mcycles as the application's per-input budget allows. iyield automatic is enabled in rollups templates (the CLI requires both yield bits in cmio mode).
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template whose guest an input can subvert: section 4 says 'Any input may take control of the firmware, the kernel, the rollup libraries, and the application. It may then run any instruction stream at any privilege level.' A single store instruction to the HTIF tohost register is enough. No special state is needed.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The closest exclusion is 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs or yields. Each costs the guest mcycles, which the application's own bound limits ... This holds as long as ... each yield costs it a bounded amount (R12).' The per-yield cost here is bounded (at most 2 MiB copied and hashed), so triage may apply this exclusion. Against that reading: the trigger is not the NUMBER of yields but a defect that multiplies the cost of EACH yield by a constant (two to three orders of magnitude), with a cost the guest does not pay in mcycles, since it declares 2 MiB without writing them. Section 8 lists exactly that under High ('multiply the worst-case cost ... by a constant factor'), and the exclusion does not cover it. If the exclusion is read as covering every bounded per-yield cost, the result is Out of scope.

2 Role: the PRT player is Support (AUDIT.md component table). Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator or a tool that computes claims.' The emulator API it calls (receive_cmio_request) works as documented and is not the defect. The emulator's own collector pays about 30 us per yield (local) on the same guest.

3 High/Medium cases: in the honest-operator role this matches the High case 'A defect that lets the guest ... multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor, compared with the same operation without the defect, while staying within what the deployment was sized for. A cost that the specified semantics require is not a defect.' The operation is 'a part of a claim' (R12). The semantics do not require the cost: section 4 says 'The outputs Merkle root, the output payloads, and every other yield reason are opaque guest data that the state merely commits to', and R12 says outputs storage is not on the honest operator's path ('Keeping outputs to prove them later is not on the honest operator's path', section 8). Measured factor: about 174x local and about 470x over JSON-RPC on the same yields. If the factor pushes the claim past what the deployment was sized for, the role rating would be Critical ('An operation listed in R12 whose worst-case cost a guest can make ... larger than what the deployment was sized for'). Either way it is Medium for a support component.

4 Critical: not applicable to a support component (capped at Medium by section 3). A production validator that read and hashed every output payload inline on its claim path would rate High or Critical by the clauses quoted in step 3.

5 Low: not reached unless triage applies the yield exclusion of step 1 (then Out of scope) or decides the cost is required. Two facts decide it: whether 'each yield costs it a bounded amount' excuses any bounded per-yield cost, and whether reading output payloads counts as required semantics for an operator that also proves outputs.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support stand-in for a High constant-factor R12 defect); Out of scope if triage reads the outputs/yields exclusion as covering every bounded per-yield cost
candidates.threat_to_goal: The goal assumes the honest operator computes its claim and responds within the clocks the deployment was sized for (A7, R4 'cannot respond in time' is a completeness failure). A guest that spends its per-input mcycles on payload-declaring yields makes the player's claim pass run at about 2.6 ms per mcycle (local) or about 30 ms per mcycle (JSON-RPC), instead of about 15-65 us per mcycle for the emulator's collection of the same yields. That is a 170-470x multiplier that a sizing based on the emulator's own costs does not foresee. It compounds with the player's non-preemptive whole-input idle steps (R1-A7-3). The longer it takes to build the claim, the later the honest claim joins, so the honest claim can miss its clock.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFYIELD/measure2.lua with the bare-metal guest yield-loop.S, built with bugs/harness/baremetal/build.sh. The guest is a 2-instruction loop that stores tohost = yield|automatic|TX_OUTPUT|DATA 0x200000 and writes nothing to the tx buffer. Each line is 100 yields (2 mcycles each), mcycle collector log2 period 10, after a warm-up call. 'local collect only' 30.0 us/yield. 'local collect + what prt.lua run_to_stop/on_yield_automatic does' (receive_cmio_request + keccak256 for TX_OUTPUT) 5225 us/yield. 'jsonrpc collect only' 128 us/yield. 'jsonrpc collect + player receive' 60512 us/yield. A separate run (measure.lua) split the cost: JSON-RPC receive alone about 57.8 ms/yield, local receive alone about 0.74 ms/yield, keccak of 2 MiB about 4 ms. For context, the uarch collector costs about 11 ms per mcycle, but the player's run_next_input pass only uses the mcycle collector.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test with the bare-metal builder. Build a template guest that accepts its first request, then on each advance input runs K=50 iterations of a tohost store with yield|automatic|TX_OUTPUT|0x200000, writing nothing to the tx buffer, and accepts with the empty outputs root. Build a player (prt.new_player or new_stored_player) and run its run_next_input on one input. Wrap the pair machine's receive_cmio_request through a proxy table, or a counting metatable that delegates every other method, to sum #data returned during the claim pass. Required behavior: the bytes of tx-buffer payload the claim computation reads do not depend on the guest-declared DATA. Assert total_bytes_read <= 32 * (number of manual yields), for example. That exits 1 today (50 * 2 MiB) and 0 once the claim pass stops reading payloads, or reads them only when outputs are actually wanted, or limits them to what the guest could have written. A timing variant: assert that run_next_input on this input takes at most 4x as long as collect_mcycle_root_hashes over the same mcycles on a fork.

not_covered: Dave/rollups-contracts handling of guest outputs beyond reading (Application.executeOutput/validateOutput decoding of guest-chosen output bytes, outputs larger than a transaction can carry): not audited

machine-guest-tools (libcmt emit/finish/gio, rollup CLI, rollup-http-server) consistency between the bytes they hash for the outputs tree and the bytes/length they declare in tohost: not re-read (round-1 GUEST hunters covered libcmt)

Uarch and Solidity (UArchStep/UArchReset/SendCmioResponse) equivalence for HTIF device writes with unusual tohost values (unknown devices, cmd >= 64, halt with DATA bit0 = 0, disabled iyield bits): only read the shared C++ device code, no differential run

Console bytes: host cost of a guest printing a newline every mcycle with to_stdout/every_line inside collect_mcycle_root_hashes (one write syscall per line) was reasoned about (below the per-yield worst case), not measured; R1-R14-1 covers to_buffer

JSON-RPC server/client paths for receive_cmio_request were read (bounded allocation, length checks); not fuzzed; cm_receive_cmio_request with a non-null buffer of length 0 silently acts as a length query (API nit, not reported)

The cartesi-machine CLI's per-yield behavior (reads every automatic-yield payload, prints a line per yield, writes one file per report and per output, asserts #data == 32 on accept): dev tool, reported only as sharing candidate 1's pattern

PRT player store_first_epoch_checkpoint refuses a template whose tx buffer holds a non-empty outputs root (the manual mentions non-genesis templates for the CLI); judged intended for a genesis-only Dave deployment, not reported
The vg.lua verification-game player and the referee model's transport were not examined under this angle

Interaction of automatic yields with the player restart/persistence path (stored pairs, machine cache) and with bundle replays (collect_mcycle_bundle/collect_uarch_cycle_bundle) was read only; those use the null builder and do not read payloads
Halt payloads and exception payloads in the bridge/stageTournamentResult path: read only (the bridge goes terminal when the settled state is not an accepted yield, which matches A5)
